Name: Abderus
Description: aided Heracles during his eighth labour and was killed by the Mares of Diomedes

Name: Achilles
Description: hero of the Trojan War and a central character in Homer's Iliad

Name: Aeneas
Description: a hero of the Trojan War and progenitor of the Roman people

Name: Ajax the Great
Description: a hero of the Trojan War and king of Salamis

Name: Ajax the Lesser
Description: a hero of the Trojan War and leader of the Locrian army

Name: Amphitryon
Description: Theban general who rescued Thebes from the Teumessian fox; his wife was Alcmene, mother of Heracles

Name: Antilochus
Description: Son of Nestor sacrificed himself to save his father in the Trojan War along with other deeds of valor

Name: Bellerophon
Description: hero who slew the Chimera

Name: Castor
Description: the mortal Dioscuri twin; after Castor's death, his immortal brother Pollux shared his divinity with him in order that they might remain together

Name: Chrysippus
Description: a divine hero of Elis

Name: Daedalus
Description: creator of the labyrinth and great inventor, until King Minos trapped him in his own creation.

Name: Diomedes
Description: a king of Argos and hero of the Trojan War

Name: Eleusis
Description: eponymous hero of the town of Eleusis

Name: Eunostus
Description: a Boeotian hero

Name: Ganymede
Description: Trojan hero and lover of Zeus, who was given immortality and appointed cup-bearer to the gods

Name: Hector
Description: hero of the Trojan War and champion of the Trojan people

Name: Icarus
Description: the son of the master craftsman Daedalus

Name: Iolaus
Description: nephew of Heracles who aided his uncle in one of his Labors

Name: Jason
Description: leader of the Argonauts

Name: Meleager
Description: a hero who sailed with the Argonauts and killed the Calydonian Boar

Name: Odysseus
Description: a hero and king of Ithaca whose adventures are the subject of Homer's Odyssey; he also played a key role during the Trojan War

Name: Orpheus
Description: a legendary musician and poet who attempted to retrieve his dead wife from the Underworld

Name: Pandion
Description: the eponymous hero of the Attic tribe Pandionis, usually assumed to be one of the legendary Athenian kings Pandion I or Pandion II.

Name: Perseus
Description: son of Zeus and the founder-king of Mycenae and slayer of the Gorgon Medusa

Name: Theseus
Description: son of Poseidon and a king of Athens and slayer of the Minotaur
